review_candidates.title: Program Analyst, HIV
review_candidates.description: The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems. CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally. At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work http//www.clintonhealthaccess.org CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture. Position Summary The Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI) is seeking a highly motivated Program Analyst to provide programmatic leadership, supervision, coordination, performance monitoring and stakeholder engagement for the Key Population (KP) Peer Navigators Program. The program supports the identification, tracing, re-engagement, and linkage to HIV prevention and treatment services of female sex workers (FSW) and men who have sex with men (MSM) who were lost from Kenya Health Information System (KHIS) records following the 2025 donor funding transition across the six project counties following the 2025 donor funding transitions. This is a program supervision, coordination, and engagement role. It does not include direct client tracing, peer education, or case management, which are carried out by community-based peer educators under the supervision of Ministry of Health Community Health Assistants (CHAs). The Program Analyst instead provides programmatic oversight of the peer educator cadre through the CHA supervisory structure, coordinates with county and national stakeholders, and ensures activities are delivered efficiently, on schedule, within budget, and in compliance with Ministry of Health and donor requirements. Provide day-to-day programmatic oversight of the KP Peer Navigators Program across the six project counties, ensuring activities are delivered on time, within budget, and in line with the approved work plan and cost-effectiveness (BOTEC) targets. Coordinate with the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) supervising peer educators to track progress against monthly tracing and linkage targets, monthly facility-level micro-planning meetings including biannual supervision and mentorship visits. Monitor program performance, identify underperformance, bottlenecks, and county-specific risks such as political will for peer educator absorption, KHIS reporting gaps, and facility readiness, and escalate them to the Senior Director, Infectious Diseases, with recommended solutions. Serve as CHAI's primary liaison with the County Health Management Teams (CHMTs) in the six project counties, leading county entry meetings and working with county KP coordinators and facility in-charges to resolve linkage barriers raised in biweekly joint review meetings. Support county-level advocacy for the recognition and absorption of well-performing peer educators as special community health promoters within county community health systems. Represent CHAI with NASCOP, the Ministry of Health, and other national KP stakeholders, including the program inception meeting and technical working groups, and liaise with other implementing partners and donors such as the Global Fund GC8 program and PEPFAR-supported partners to avoid duplication. Coordinate with NASCOP's data and KHIS teams to secure facility-level lost-client lists and support restoration of KP reporting in the six project counties. Oversee data quality and program tracking, including monthly data-quality audits comparing peer educator registers against KHIS and facility records, and maintenance of the cohort loss, implementation timeline, and budget tracking tools. Track monitoring and evaluation indicators, including ART and prevention re-engagement, KHIS report rate, facility dataset activation, and retention by service-delivery model; prepare monthly and quarterly reports; and support the end-of-grant evaluation of which service-delivery model best retains each KP group under domestic financing. Ensure adherence to ethical standards, safeguarding principles, data protection requirements, and confidentiality protocols in all program activities involving key population clients and health records. Support operational research, assessments, and evaluations aimed at identifying effective service-delivery approaches for re-engagement and retention of key populations under domestic financing models. Support budget tracking for peer educator stipends, training, supervision, and micro-planning cost lines, and prepare disbursement requests and expenditure reconciliation with CHAI finance in line with donor requirements. Perform any other duty as assigned by the supervisor Bachelor's degree in public health, social sciences, monitoring and evaluation, or a related field. At least one year of experience coordinating or supervising HIV or public health programs in Kenya, including experience with key population programming. Demonstrated experience engaging county and national government stakeholders, particularly County Health Management Teams and NASCOP or similar national programs. Working knowledge of the Kenya Health Information System (KHIS), the Community Health Strategy, and key population service-delivery models. Experience with program monitoring and evaluation, including data quality assurance and indicator tracking. Experience supporting budget tracking and donor reporting is an advantage. Cultural competence and sensitivity in working with key population communities, and awareness of the ethical and confidentiality considerations involved. Skills And Competencies Excellent written and verbal communication. Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills, particularly with county and national government counterparts. Data analysis and reporting skills, including familiarity with KHIS or similar health information systems. Program and project coordination skills, with the ability to manage multiple county-level workstreams at once. Sound judgment and problem-solving ability, with the capacity to work independently. A high degree of discretion and confidentiality. #jobreference1 #region3

review_candidates.description: Term: Full time, initial term 1 year                                                                              Location: Équateur Province, DRC (Work a min of 4 overlapping hours with the North America Central time zone)   Project Background The Integrating Gender Outcomes-Based Financing into a JREDD+ Program in Équateur Province, DRC grant is piloting an innovative model that integrates verified gender impact outcomes into a Jurisdictional REDD+ (JREDD+) Program in the Équateur Province, DRC and seeking to attract outcome-based finance that complements climate finance. While JREDD+ programs are effective at mobilizing climate finance to reduce deforestation, they do not explicitly measure or fund women’s contributions or activities that benefit women, despite women being central actors in forest conservation and community livelihoods. In the Équateur Province, forest-dependent communities manage extensive forest areas through Community Forest Concessions (CFCLs). Within these systems, women play a critical role in subsistence agriculture and fuelwood, and Non-Timber Forest Product (NTFP) collection. However, they face persistent structural barriers, including limited access to income-generating opportunities, restricted control over assets, exclusion from decision-making processes, and disproportionate unpaid labor burdens. These factors limit the effectiveness and durability of forest conservation efforts. Inclusive, equitable programs improve compliance, reduce conflict, and bolster environmental outcomes. Despite this, existing REDD+ financing channels often do not explicitly recognize the important role women play in forest conservation. This pilot aims to address that gap by designing a Gender Based Outcome Finance Program embedded within a JREDD+ Program, using the W+ Standard [1] to define, measure, and verify outcomes across key domains related to women’s empowerment (access to income and assets, time savings, and leadership). The pilot will design a Gender Based Program that benefits approximately 4,556 women across 28 villages in five CFCLs, covering over 115,000 hectares of threatened forest area. This pilot will be co-designed with local partners and beneficiaries through participatory consultations, Theory of Change (TOC) workshops, and capacity building sessions. Outcomes for the 12-month grant period include: Conduct community consultation with gender focus. Design Gender-focused activities through a participatory process. Define baseline for gender outcomes under the W+ Standard. Develop the Monitoring plan in accordance with the W+ Standard. Develop the W+ Project Description Document (PDD).  Pilot the demand for Gender Based Outcome Finance. Responsibilities The Local Project Coordinator will provide technical support and coordination for the engagement with Concessions Forestières des Communautés Locales (Local Community Forest Concessions-CFCLs). This will be overseeing and supporting the implementation partners (CFCL operators) to design gender focused activities, collect field data and implement activities to meet W+ Standard requirements. This role will lead the coordination between the Terra Global (International team), implementing partners, and the project participants (CFCLs) in the Équateur Province. The main activities to be implemented by the Local Project Coordinator will include but are not limited to the following: Coordinate Field Activities Lead coordination with all local implementation partners, communities, and government stakeholders so that key project activities are implemented on schedule and under budget. Lead and facilitate participatory consultation sessions with communities and partners to gather inputs and feedback and process those inputs in project plans, Theory of Change (TOC) documentation, and other project deliverables. Facilitate inclusive sessions in which women and other under-represented groups can meaningfully participate. Document in-field activities to demonstrate results of engagement processes and FPIC Support data collection to define the baseline conditions for gender outcomes in the project areas. Serve as the day-to-day point of contact person between Terra Global and local partners. Assess and communicate risks, delays, and partner needs to the Terra Global International team in a timely manner. Coordinate Office-based Activities Support and act as a liaison for Terra Global and the project including: Support all partners to follow best practice communication with Terra Global, including scheduling weekly calls and meetings. Contribute to sections of technical reports, including the W+ Standard Project Description Document (PDD). Support fiscal management procedures for the Équateur Province W+ Pilot. Support the procurement of goods for local partners and participants. Support translation for the international team both remotely and in country (French, local language(s), and English). Ensure consistent and timely flow of information and data from the field to the Terra Global International team. Engage with the provincial and national government and identify governmental focal points within relevant agencies for the success of the Project. Gender-Focused Programming Provide gender-specific expertise to design gender-sensitive and gender-focused initiatives, in collaboration with partners and communities. Help partners and communities identify opportunities and barriers for women in the project context, and reflect these in activity design. Support the identification and documentation of women’s empowerment outcomes consistent with W+ Standard requirements. Lead Monitoring Data Collection Work closely with the local partners and local communities, lead field activities to gather, organize and store field-based data for monitoring the Project. These monitoring data needs tasks include: Collect and report operational data on project activities, using templates and methods required under the grant, W+ Standard, and Terra Global. Maintain organized, accurate records of activities, participants, site visits, and meetings. Prepare regular progress updates and field reports for Terra Global and to fulfill grant reporting requirements. Secondary Responsibilities: Jurisdictional REDD+ Program Support The LPC will also support the associated jurisdictional REDD+ Program, which is under development. Time spent on this work is secondary to the W+ pilot. The tasks are as follow: Collaborate with partners and stakeholders on key REDD+ deliverables, including work plans, budgets, and assessments. Carry out other field work for the REDD+ Program as required. Share field insights between the W+ Pilot and the REDD+ Program to ensure the two are aligned.   Qualifications Required DRC national, based in Équateur Province, with knowledge of forest management and the ability to travel frequently to remote rural areas Minimum 5 years of work experience in program management and monitoring, including coordination of multiple partners and activities, natural resource management and/or REDD+ projects Expertise in gender and/or community development work in DRC or a similar context Fluency in Lingala, French and English, with strong verbal and written communication skills Home-based is in Équateur Province Proficiency with MS Office programs, especially Excel and Word Experience on drafting progress and monitoring reports Familiarity with mobile-based monitoring tools and smartphone applications for field data collection (Kobo, SMART, Survey123 or others) Experience in capacity building, facilitation, and promoting adoption of tools and practices at the community level Demonstrated success in building strong relationships with government institutions, community organizations, and local stakeholders Able to work independently and self-manage deadlines and deliverables Exceptional verbal/written communication skills, especially working across cultures Access to regular electricity and internet (as is reasonable within DRC’s infrastructure) Ability to travel extensively throughout the province and spend 1-2 weeks per month in the field. Valid driver’s license and access to a vehicle or motorbike suitable for fieldwork (travel costs will be reimbursed per Terra’s travel policies) Interpersonal Skills: Strong interpersonal skills and ability to build trust with women, communities, government officials, and implementation partners. Cultural sensitivity, humility, and respect for local knowledge and customs. Excellent facilitation and active-listening skills, including with underrepresented groups. Diplomacy and sound judgment when navigating competing priorities or sensitive issues. Collaborative working style across field-based and international teams. Strong organization, adaptability, initiative, and practical problem-solving. Ability to communicate complex information clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences. Commitment to confidentiality, safeguarding, inclusion, and ethical conduct. Desirable Demonstrated and successful past performance building relationships and negotiating with governmental authorities (local, regional and national), non-governmental organizations (NGOs); Experience implementing community-based projects in field settings, including with local governance structures Comfortable working across cultures and maintaining professional relationships with diverse partners Accepting resumes until position is filled. Compensation will be basis on local rates for similar positions. Compensation Range: USD $25,000 - $35,000 per year as consultant

Challenges such as cost efficiency per square foot, logistics-optimized locations, and seamless technology integration have made it clear that a new approach is needed. We believe the future of foodservice and commerce lies in purpose-built infrastructure designed for speed, accuracy, and scalability. That’s why Namaa was established—to power the next generation of digital food and quick commerce ecosystems across the Middle East. Our ecosystem is driven by a portfolio of specialized business units, including KitchenPark , CloudRetail , and Profood Properties , each playing a key role in enabling brands to grow and thrive in an increasingly on-demand world. Collaborate with stakeholders across different departments to understand training needs and create content that supports team objectives and business processes. Help translate complex information, policies, and processes into clear, practical, and easy-to-understand training materials. Support employee onboarding by preparing learning resources and assisting with training initiatives for new joiners. We’re constantly reimagining our industry, creating new products, and refining our processes, and we do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week. Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

While based in one IJM program office within the region, the Photojournalist will travel significantly across multiple countries in-region to capture stories, support media opportunities and strengthen regional storytelling capacity. This role supports regional storytelling efforts while actively contributing to campaign-ready content aligned with organizational messaging, advocacy, fundraising, social media and media engagement priorities. The Photojournalist will help surface stories with strong digital and media potential, creating content suited for social platforms, editorial environments and global communication channels. Applicants must submit a portfolio demonstrating strong visual storytelling capabilities across photography and/or video, including experience capturing sensitive stories with dignity and emotional depth. Experience working in cross-cultural environments, preferably across Latin America, with the ability to build relationships and collaborate effectively with local, regional, and global stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to independently manage story development, interview facilitation, logistics coordination, and editorial decision-making in complex field environments. Strong skills in creating compelling written, photographic, and video content for diverse audiences and communication channels. Knowledge of digital storytelling trends, social media platforms, and audience engagement strategies. Excellent interviewing, communication, and relationship-building skills. Experience applying ethical, trauma-informed storytelling practices and working with vulnerable populations. Background in human rights, international development, or mission-driven organizations preferred. Demonstrated commitment to advocacy for vulnerable populations and ethical storytelling principles. Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to work resiliently and professionally in emotionally challenging environments while exercising empathy and sound judgment. Willingness to travel for field visits, content-gathering assignments, and regional storytelling projects. Advanced written communication in English; multilingual ability is a requirement. This position requires availability to travel, across Latin America. Application Please submit an application letter explaining your interest in working at IJM (including salary expectations) and your CV in one document, through the “Simple Application” button. IJM upholds strict safeguarding principles and maintains zero tolerance for violations of the Safeguarding Policy, the Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy, and the Code of Ethics. Candidate selection is based on technical competency criteria. Recruitment, selection, and hiring are subject to an evaluation of the candidate’s alignment with IJM’s values and to thorough background checks, including police records and references.

If you're passionate about healthcare, strategic account management, and delivering meaningful impact for patients and healthcare systems, we'd love to hear from you. Drive Patient Access Play a critical role in expanding access to innovative Anti-Infectives therapies and ensuring patients receive the treatments they need. High-Impact Stakeholder Engagement Build meaningful relationships with healthcare decision-makers, pharmacists, clinicians, procurement bodies, and regional healthcare institutions. Commercial and Strategic Influence Contribute directly to business performance by identifying opportunities, overcoming access barriers, and developing customer-centric solutions. Identify access opportunities and implement customer-centric solutions that support the product access strategy and commercial objectives. Manage and grow relationships with key stakeholders including hospitals, healthcare authorities, procurement bodies, and clinical decision-makers. Make informed business decisions to maximize commercial opportunities while safeguarding Mundipharma's long-term market position. Drive implementation of national and regional strategic initiatives within assigned accounts. Support territory segmentation and targeting to ensure appropriate resource allocation and customer engagement. Map and identify strategic accounts and key stakeholders to support both current and future product launches. Provide valuable field insights to support territory action planning and market development strategies. Market Access & Brand Positioning Support the positioning and listing of assigned products within regional formularies, treatment pathways, and reference documents. Contribute to increasing awareness and recognition of the Mundipharma portfolio and corporate brand across selected accounts. Partner with internal stakeholders to develop strategies that improve product availability and utilization. Facilitate effective stakeholder engagement to support patient access objectives. Competitive Intelligence & Business Insights Monitor market developments, competitor activities, customer trends, and healthcare policy changes. Identify opportunities and potential risks that may impact market performance. Provide regular market intelligence and actionable insights to internal stakeholders. Support strategic planning through robust analysis of customer and territory dynamics. Compliance & Operational Excellence Perform all activities in accordance with company policies, compliance requirements, and the Farmaindustria Code of Practice. Maintain accurate, timely, and complete records of customer interactions and account activities within CRM systems. Ensure high-quality reporting and territory management practices. Act as a role model for ethical business conduct and compliance excellence. Essential Qualifications What We're Looking For Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Biology, Biotechnology, Healthcare, or a related scientific discipline. Fluency in Italian and good working proficiency in English. Valid driving licence and willingness to travel extensively within the assigned territory. Experience Proven successful experience as a Key Account Manager within the pharmaceutical or life sciences industry. Demonstrated track record of achieving commercial objectives and driving account growth. Experience within Anti-Infectives, Fungal Diseases, HIV, or related therapeutic areas. Experience working with hospitals, regional healthcare systems, and institutional stakeholders. Strong knowledge and experience using CRM reporting and account management systems. Excellent communication and presentation skills. Ability to confidently discuss complex medical and scientific concepts with healthcare professionals. Strong stakeholder management and influencing abilities. Customer-focused mindset with strong problem-solving skills. Excellent organizational, analytical, and business planning skills. review_candidates.title: International Expansion
review_candidates.description: About Us At Axle Energy, we’re building the infrastructure that will underpin the decarbonised energy system. Our software moves energy usage to times when electricity is cheap and green, by controlling vehicle charging, heating systems, inverters and home batteries. We control hundreds of thousands of energy assets. We’re building in a legacy industry and moving gigawatt-hours of electrons in the real world, but we operate at lightning speed, and we’re growing the team to meet customer demand. We’re proud to be supported by world-leading investors, including Energize Capital and Accel. Read more about what we’re building here . We’re looking for a commercially sharp, highly autonomous operator to drive Axle’s commercial success in the German market. Axle has quickly become the leader in our operational markets, and we’re now looking to expand our reach internationally. Our goal is to become the go-to platform for energy flexibility globally, and we’re hiring the person to make that happen. This role will assess Axle’s participation in German markets and business models from first principles: diving deep into regulations, modelling revenue-per-asset, and trialling new propositions at pace. You speak German and fluent English. Other European languages are also an asset. What you will be doing Owning Axle’s commercial results in the German market: pipeline, revenue and partner success Winning new customers end-to-end, from first conversation through to commercial close, and setting partners up to generate meaningful revenue Driving go-to-market execution with partners, including value propositions, pricing, customer segmentation and launch strategy Building the zero-to-one of the business through partnerships. You’ll be on the phone (and on the ground) with utilities/retailers, potential clients and grid operators, creating and disproving hypotheses as quickly as possible Continuing to sharpen our view of where the value is and which markets and business models are accessible to us Building lasting relationships with grid operators and the regulator, so that Axle is well positioned as the market evolves Acting as the conduit between partners and engineering, creating fast, structured feedback loops that turn field insights into product improvements As such, we are looking for a “full-stack operator” who can process highly technical information, ramp up commercial value, and accelerate us into new markets. You might have previous experience in one or more of the activities above, but we are more interested in your growth potential than your domain-specific expertise. We are looking for people who have built things, developed new relationships, and helped get big projects over the line in complex environments. This is an opportunity to repeatedly deliver first-of-a-kind projects across the world, become a domain expert, and work at the bleeding edge of global electrification. What’s In It For You This is a 12 month fixed-term contract. Compensation is highly competitive and dependent on experience. We operate with a deliberately flat structure and aim to keep pay equitable across the company, with a 1:1 median ratio between founder and team compensation. Bi-annual retreats to strengthen team connection & shared purpose. You’ll be based in the Germany. To maximise collaboration, we ask that you spend ~1 week per month working from our London office. The opportunity to directly shape the future of energy markets and accelerate the transition to a low-carbon world. We are extremely keen to build a diverse team, and we’re particularly eager to hear from candidates who don't fit the traditional role stereotypes. If you’re motivated by our mission, please do reach out, even if you feel you might not ‘check all the boxes’. Interview process Initial interview Take-home exercise Final interview (in-person) Offer, references, and welcome to the team!

The GSAD is the main liaison between the study team and the Clinical Program Team (CPT) starting with study handover through to close-out and archiving. The GSAD is accountable to the CPT for the delivery of a study according to agreed upon timelines, budget, and quality standards by ensuring an effective partnership and teamwork within study team and/or external partners. The GSAD leads the study team and/or study oversight team in accordance with the study team operating model, current clinical trial regulations (e.g. ICH GCP), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), policies and best practices (e.g. guidelines) and in line with values and behaviours. Essential Functions Lead, provide guidance and delegate appropriately to a cross-functional study team or oversee outsourced delivery activities to ensure the clinical study progresses as planned, driving achievement of milestones according to timelines, budget and quality standards. May hold accountability and/or oversight of several studies. Lead and facilitate communication across all functions, including external partners and service providers. Lead and conduct investigator meetings and other study related meetings. Provide input into and hold accountability for the development of essential study level documents (i.e., Clinical Study Protocol (CSP) through to Clinical Study Report (CSR)) in accordance with relevant SOPs. Ensure all external service providers (i.e., Contract Research Organizations (CROs), central laboratories, IXRS, ePRO, etc.) engaged at the study level are performing to contracted goals and timelines/budget and that adequate oversight is documented and any issues are escalated appropriately. May participate in vendor selection activities. Develop and maintain relevant study plans including required input into study level quality and risk management planning (e.g., risk-based quality management, proactive risk and contingency plans, etc.) ensuring that the risk response strategies and issue escalation pathways are clear to the entire study team Accountable for ensuring that information in all systems utilized at a study-level (e.g. ACCORD/ABACUS, PharmaCM, etc.) are current and accurate. Oversee study level performance against agreed upon plans, milestones and key performance indicators (KPIs, quality and operational) by using company tracking systems and project timelines and communicate any risks to timelines and/or quality to CPT and sDSM/DSM along with proposed mitigations Identify and report quality issues that have occurred within the study in accordance with relevant SOP and collaborate with all functions as necessary to overcome barriers and achieve milestones; proactively communicate findings and corrective action plans (CAPAs) to relevant stakeholders (e.g. CPT, quality assurance staff, functional line management, etc.) Oversee Trial Master File (TMF) completion in accordance with relevant SOPs, including ensuring the TMF plan and Expected Document List (EDL) are in place and that QC activities are performed on an ongoing basis to ensure TMF completeness at all times Ensure timely compliance with company-wide governance controls (e.g., Delegation of Authority, Sunshine Act, financial system attestations, Clinical Trial Transparency) The GSAD is responsible for study budget re-forecasting following initial budget estimate provided by the CPT and accountable for study budget management through the study lifecycle and for providing budget progress reports to the CPT including any financial risks and mitigation plans (as part of the ongoing study change control process) Ensure studies are inspection-ready at all times, according to ICH-GCP and SOP and relevant policies/guidelines; GSAD is the primary Study Management point-of-contact in the event of an audit or inspection Provide regular feedback on individual performance to the study team members and their line managers to support their professional development; may mentor less experienced colleagues Work on non-drug project work such as being a Study Management representative in process improvements and/or leading improvement projects as discussed and agreed upon with their manage May act as Subject Matter Expert for a particular process or system within Study Management.
